evidence.source: 香港教育局 字源考釋
evidence.field: 字形流變 / 字形解說
evidence.text: The account describes oracle-bone 上 as a short horizontal marker above a longer horizontal line representing a horizon; it says later bronze and small-seal forms altered the upper stroke to distinguish the character from 二, while the modern standard form adds a dot. This is a source analysis of an indicative graph, not an artifact inspection.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 上

evidence.source: 中央研究院 漢字構形資料庫
evidence.text: The entry describes the oracle-bone graph as two horizontal strokes: the lower, longer stroke represents a horizon and the upper, shorter one marks above. It says the upper stroke became vertical in a later form to avoid confusion with 二. This account differs from CUHK’s description of a curved baseline.
evidence.title: 漢字「上」：字形演變

evidence.text: The search result for the inspected character page describes oracle-bone 上 as a short stroke over a curved line. This supports the curved-baseline alternative but does not settle the variation across individual early forms. It reports inscription examples elsewhere in the dossier; those artifact examples were not independently checked in this run.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.text: The supplied exact local rows give Unihan kMandarin 上 = shàng. The three supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 lexical rows are MC dzyangX / OC *Cə-daŋʔ (‘ascend’), MC dzyangX / OC *m-daŋʔ (‘to put up’), and MC dzyangH / OC *daŋʔ-s (‘top, above’). Keep these as separate lexical entries. They do not evidence the graph’s formation or sound changes.

search_audit.query: 上 甲骨文 金文 字形 指事 字源 上 字 古文字; Commons ACC-s00008 上-seal SVG exact file
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Education Bureau page and Sinica character evolution page. The hinted ACC-s00008 description page and Unicode character record were inaccessible. The exact 上-seal Commons page was inspected.

search_audit.query: 上 oracle bone inscription earliest attestation Shang oracle 上帝; 上 字 甲骨文 曲线 横画 两说 字源 甲骨文 金文
search_audit.outcome: Search surfaced CUHK’s curved-baseline account and an oracle-style Commons image. Inspected the Commons page and its reuse terms; no inspected primary artifact image adjudicated the two graphic descriptions.

gaps: The character is analyzed as an indicative graph, not a compound: no semantic or phonetic components are proposed.

The inspected paleographic sources agree on a short marker placed above a reference line but differ on whether early examples have a curved baseline or two horizontal lines. No primary inscription image was inspected to resolve this variation.
Inscription examples and dates in the dossier are reports from secondary epigraphic sources. This run did not independently inspect the cited artifacts or establish a precise dated semantic sequence.

The earliest securely discussed graph form here is oracle-bone 上, conventionally associated with Late Shang inscriptions; no earlier dated occurrence of this specific graph was established in the inspected sources.
The transition from spatial ‘above’ to ‘superior’, ‘ruler’, or verbal ‘ascend/send up’ is not chronologically established here. Do not infer this order from a gloss list.

The exact official Unicode character page for U+4E0A was inaccessible. The local kMandarin and Baxter–Sagart rows are preserved as supplied but are not claimed as independently verified through the official page.
The ACC-s00008 Commons page was inaccessible, so that lead was not selected. No reuse terms for repeated bulk materials were investigated; the selected assets are character-specific Commons images.

items.selection_reason: Pairs an identified later script style with the oracle-style candidate and shows graphic history as a change in representation, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: These are modern digital redrawings labeled by script style, not photographs or direct facsimiles of dated artifacts; captions should preserve that distinction.
The two Commons candidates help compare script styles but do not adjudicate the disagreement over whether the earliest baseline was curved.
